Everyone does this to a degree, but imagine whatever you'd consider to be excessive. Examples:

  • Couldn't imagine why.
  • Wish I knew.
  • Should've done better.
  • Regretted that.
  • Love you.

Notice how the subject of the sentence becomes ambiguous? It's like using language to distance yourself from the actions you're discussing -- a version of compartmentalization.

So dissociating yourself from negative actions may act like a defense mechanism. But if you do it in excess, then you may completely forget it was your action to begin with. This would lead to an accumulated inability to acknowledge, and maybe even identify, your own faults. Ultimately this could carry over to all sorts of actions.
